title: Format weights and compare their magnitudes
description: You build an equation string and normalize absolute feature weights for a printed report.

steps.description: You pair weights[0] with feature names and format each coefficient. join combines the terms, and a separate formatted bias completes the equation string.
You take absolute weights and divide each by their sum. Multiplication by 100 expresses those magnitude shares as percentages.

steps.question: Do these percentages depend on each observation's feature values?
steps.answer: This calculation uses only weights[0]. It normalizes coefficient magnitudes without multiplying by observation values.

steps.description: You print each feature name beside its normalized share. The recording gives Payment History the largest share of the absolute weights.
